description: About Us We are a stealth-stage fund and tech startup operating at the intersection of alternative markets and quantitative strategy. Backed by experienced operators and growing quickly, we are building the infrastructure to scale a high-performance, data-driven business. We have found something that works. What we have not yet built is the machine that runs it at ten times the current volume, and the founder is currently the machine. The Role Every department in this company reports to the founder today. That is why this role exists. As COO you own the internal engine end to end: how work enters the business, how it moves through delivery, and whether it comes out the other side at the quality we promised. The founder moves to strategy, capital and external growth. You take everything else. This is not a caretaker role for a machine that already runs. Several of the departments you will own do not have a manual, a metric or in some cases a manager. You are being hired to build those, in order, while the current volume keeps flowing. What You'll Do Take the operating load. Become the person the company runs through, so the founder is not the escalation point for eight departments. Own throughput and the quality that comes with it. We need to multiply the number of people we take through our delivery pipeline each week without the failure rate rising. Both halves of that sentence are the job. Build the operating cadence. A weekly meeting structure with real accountability, quarterly goals with named owners, and a company scorecard of eight to twelve numbers. Most of those numbers do not exist yet. You will define them and then make them true. Write the operating manual. We have almost no documented processes. You will map the core ones, get them written down, and cut how long it takes a new hire to become useful. Make quality measurable. Nothing in the business currently logs mistakes. You will change that across delivery, support and review, and use what it tells you. Consolidate the tooling. Real-time visibility of the whole business in one place, rather than the several disconnected systems people half-trust today. Hire and keep operators. Several senior seats are open and more are coming. The quality of the people underneath you is the ceiling on everything above. Open new markets. Two geographic expansions are in flight. The blocker on both is operational, not technical. You see the business as connected loops and you go to work on the actual constraint rather than the loudest complaint You reach for process and automation before you reach for headcount You are a strong, direct writer. description: Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Ghana. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early. 1. Background Ghana hosts refugees and asylum seekers from neighboring countries, including Côte d’Ivoire, Togo and Burkina Faso. In recent years, insecurity in the Sahel region, alongside climate-related pressures and intercommunal tensions, has contributed to increased displacement and cross-border movements, particularly affecting northern Ghana. Within these populations, young people aged 18–35 face a range of barriers to education, skills development, employment and economic participation. These may include disrupted educational pathways, limited access to vocational training, difficulties accessing formal employment, documentation requirements, financial constraints and social exclusion. Young women and youth with disabilities may experience additional barriers. These barriers may be compounded by intersecting factors such as age, gender, disability, displacement status, socioeconomic circumstances and geographic location. Gender norms, unpaid care responsibilities, safety concerns and limited accessibility may further constrain participation in education and economic opportunities. However, the circumstances of displaced youth vary considerably depending on their legal status, location, socioeconomic conditions and access to institutional support. Opportunities for inclusion are also influenced by government policies, the capacities and incentives of relevant institutions, local labour-market conditions, and the availability of education and employment services. The Mastercard Foundation, through its partnership with WUSC under the DREEM project, seeks to strengthen opportunities for refugees and displaced youth (RDPs) to access education, develop relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic life. A rapid contextual assessment is therefore proposed to consolidate existing evidence, examine the institutional and structural factors shaping RDP inclusion in Ghana, and identify practical opportunities for future programming, partnerships and policy engagement. 2. Purpose of the Assessment The assessment aims to generate practical, context-specific evidence on the barriers and opportunities affecting the inclusion of refugees and displaced youth in education, skills development, employment and broader economic participation in Ghana. It will examine the policy, institutional, socioeconomic and political economy factors shaping these opportunities, including the roles and incentives of relevant government institutions, education and training providers, private-sector actors, development partners and refugee-led organizations. description: We are seeking a highly technical, hands-on Senior Voice Engineer to join our Unified Communications and Collaboration (UC&C) Solution Engineering team. Advanced Call Flows: Troubleshoot and resolve issues in complex scenarios, including attended and blind transfers, call forking, hunt and pilot groups, conferencing, call park, shared lines, simultaneous ring, emergency calling, and cloud/hybrid routing through multiple Session Border Controllers (SBCs). Diagnostic Tooling: Use Wireshark/TShark, SBC debug and trace tools, call-control platform traces, call-detail records, and ladder diagrams to reconstruct call flows and document root cause. description: Job Type: Full-time, long-term contractor Workplace: Remote Schedule: Full-time, Monday to Friday - CT hours aligned Compensation: $1,500 - $1,800/month About Us HireHawk connects skilled professionals with remote opportunities at U.S. and Canadian companies. Preserve each client’s voice, personality, and intended meaning while removing repetition, tangents, and distractions. Add accurate captions, thoughtful framing, B-roll, punch-ins, and supporting visuals when they improve clarity or engagement, not simply to add effects. Deliver clean audio and polished, platform-ready videos, checking subtitles, visual details, and overall flow before handoff. Keep recurring content and revisions organized across 4-6 clients, maintaining approximately 3-4 completed videos per day in total within the expected turnaround. Adapt your editing style to each client rather than applying the same formula to every speaker or brand. Take initiative on next steps, flag unclear messaging or delivery risks early, and apply feedback so future edits require less direction. Requirements Must-Have: A portfolio that includes Instagram Reels and relevant talking-head, interview, podcast, founder, executive, thought-leadership, or personal-brand content. Relevant professional video editing experience. We’re targeting 3-5 years, ideally including 2+ years in social content, but candidates with 1-2 years and an exceptional portfolio are encouraged to apply. Editing ability and editorial judgment matter more than years alone or a degree. Proficiency in CapCut, with strong fundamentals in captions, pacing, framing, B-roll, punch-ins, basic audio cleanup, and finishing. description: Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Nigeria. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early. Background Nigeria hosts substantial populations of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, with displacement driven by armed conflict, insecurity, intercommunal tensions and climate-related pressures. As of 1 October 2026, available figures indicate approximately 3.7 million IDPs and 141,688 refugees and asylum seekers. Displaced youth aged 18–35 face multiple barriers to education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and economic participation. These include disrupted educational pathways, limited access to training and financial services, documentation requirements, restricted economic opportunities, and social exclusion. Young women and youth with disabilities may experience additional barriers. These barriers may be compounded by intersecting factors such as age, gender, disability, displacement status, socioeconomic circumstances and geographic location. Gender norms, unpaid care responsibilities, safety concerns and limited accessibility may further constrain participation in education and economic opportunities. However, the circumstances of refugees, asylum seekers and IDPs differ considerably, including in terms of their legal status, access to services, institutional support and opportunities for economic inclusion. These differences are also shaped by geography, local economic conditions, government policies and the capacities and incentives of institutions responsible for supporting displaced populations. The Mastercard Foundation, through its partnership with WUSC under the DREEM project, seeks to strengthen opportunities for refugees and displaced youth (RDPs) to access education, develop relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic life. In Nigeria, there is particular interest in understanding opportunities to strengthen the inclusion of internally displaced youth, alongside refugees and asylum seekers. A rapid contextual assessment is therefore proposed to consolidate existing evidence, examine the institutional and structural factors shaping RDP inclusion, and identify practical opportunities for future programming, partnerships and policy engagement. 2. Purpose of the Assessment The assessment aims to generate practical, context-specific evidence on the barriers and opportunities affecting the inclusion of refugees and internally displaced youth in Nigeria, particularly in education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and broader economic participation.It will examine the policy, institutional, socioeconomic and political economy factors shaping these opportunities, including the roles and incentives of relevant government institutions, private sector actors, development partners and refugee- and IDP-led organizations. title: Senior Growth Product Manager
description: Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call. Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data. About Us Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing. Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo. The Role You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work. Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked. We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging. What You'll Do Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them. Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads. Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first. Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own. From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. title: Territory Account Executive - Germany
description:
About Team & About Role

Rubrik helps organisations in every major industry stay resilient against cyberattacks, insider threats and operational disruption, protecting the data that hospitals, banks and public institutions depend on every day. As Territory Account Executive in Southern Germany, you’ll build business in one of Europe’s strongest industrial and financial regions, with large companies and ambitious Mittelstand firms on your doorstep. You’ll join a close-knit German team that shares deal strategy openly, backed by regional marketing, events and partner support to help you open doors.

What You’ll Do

  • Own a territory of accounts, from established Mittelstand to larger companies, and decide where your time creates the most value.
  • Tier your list and create the entry points that turn them into real opportunities.
  • Generate your own pipeline through outbound, LinkedIn, local events and partners, so that first conversations become qualified deals that protect customers against cyber risk.
  • Make the most of Rubrik’s regional marketing, events and partner activity by following up quickly on the interest it creates in your territory.
  • Run multi-stakeholder sales cycles end to end with MEDDPICC: find the budget owner, build champions and position Rubrik against the full scope of customer risk.
  • Work with Solutions Engineers, Channel Development and partners to extend your reach, and meet customers in person to build lasting relationships.
  • Learn from experienced colleagues through structured enablement and hands-on mentoring, and share what works with the German team in pipeline reviews and deal strategy sessions.
  • Feed local market insight and competitive signals back to Rubrik’s leadership to shape how we go to market in Germany.

Experience You’ll Need

  • A track record of winning new business in B2B enterprise software or SaaS, with consistent quota attainment and self-generated pipeline.
  • Experience running complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles and engaging technical, security and executive buyers.
  • Fluent German and professional English.
  • A structured approach to qualification and pipeline management, with MEDDPICC or a comparable framework.
  • Based in or near Düsseldorf, Frankfurt, Stuttgart or Munich, with willingness to travel regularly across your territory.
  • A learning mindset: you seek feedback, adapt quickly and want to keep growing with the support of a hands-on manager.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Background in cybersecurity, data protection, backup/recovery or adjacent infrastructure and cloud categories. It’s not a must, since we’ll teach you the rest.
  • Experience selling with channel partners.
  • Knowledge of the industrial, financial and Mittelstand lan
